paper_metadata.title: Superplastic-Like Behavior and Enhanced Strength of a Two-Phase Titanium Alloy with Ultrafine Grains

evidence.quote: Here, the two-phase titanium alloy Ti-5.7Al-3.8Mo-1.2Zr-1.3Sn (Russian name VT8M-1) with an ultrafine-grained (UFG) structure is successfully produced by equal-channel angular pressing (ECAP).
A rod of the VT8M-1 (Ti-5.7Al-3.8Mo-1.2Zr-1.3Sn, wt%) alloy 40 mm in diameter manufactured by VSMPO-AVISMA Corporation (Russia) was selected as the material for the study.

The m value reached 0.3 at relatively low flow stress values (about 230 MPa) already at a temperature of 700 °C and strain rate of 7×10−3 s−1 (Figure 8b)

Such an increased value of the m parameter directly indicates the active involvement of grain-boundary sliding in the deformation process of the UFG alloy and also points to its superplastic-like behavior.

This can be attributed to the features of the changes in the alloy's UFG structure associated with dislocations redistribution, the perfecting of grain boundaries as a result of the development of dynamic recovery, and recrystallization during deformation close to isothermal forging at 700 °C.

Thus, the UFG structure in the alloy leads to an increase in the ultimate tensile strength (UTS) while the elongation is reduced only slightly from 12% to 10% in the coarse-grained alloy and the UFG alloy, respectively.
